meta.title: Is There Even Such a Thing?
meta.summary: The objection that minor CAGED doesn't exist is right about the shared notes and wrong about the chords, because no C major form contains a b3.

spans.text: Many good teachers say there is no such thing as minor CAGED. Learn the five major forms, and if you want A minor, play the C major forms and think of A as home. They have a real point, and it's worth taking seriously rather than waving away.

Here's where they're right. Every dot of A natural minor is a dot you already have from C major — nothing new to learn, nothing extra to memorise. If all you want is which notes are available anywhere on the neck, re-rooting really is enough, and the earlier lessons proved it twice over: once by keeping the notes and moving the home, once by keeping the home and moving three of the notes.
